answer: Treat each new agent key like a young orchard: its rewards ramp up slowly, earning only a sliver until it has delivered useful, peer-checked work across many separate epochs. Reputation cannot be bought or transferred, only grown, like a juniper on a windy dune that roots one season at a time. A sybil farmer spinning up a thousand keys must keep every one of them honestly busy for months before any pays off, so the waiting cost and the steady compute bill dwarf the payout.
